validity.researcher_notes: sntat.ru (2020-12-11, Gazprom Transgaz Kazan 65th-anniversary piece): 'уже в 1954 году голубое топливо по подземной магистрали длиной почти 300 км дошло до столицы республики' (gas reached the capital via an underground trunk almost 300 km long) for the ORIGINAL 1954 line, then separately: 'в 1963 году со строительством второй ветки газопровода «Миннибаево — Казань» протяженностью 285 км' (in 1963, construction of the SECOND branch/line of the Minnibaevo-Kazan pipeline, 285 km long) -- i.e. 285 km is stated as the SECOND line's own length, not the first's. GEM currently records LengthKnown=285.00 on BOTH P2340 (this row, the 1954 line) and P5744 (the 1963 line) -- for P5744 this is well-supported (matches sntat.ru exactly), but for P2340/this row it appears to be the wrong line's figure copied over. energybase.ru's separate combined-object page gives a third, different figure (164 km) for its single 'Minnibaevo-Kazan' object, which does not resolve the question (that object conflates both lines' construction/commissioning years into one record, so its length figure cannot be confidently assigned to either individual nitka).

validity.researcher_notes: GENUINE, WELL-EVIDENCED EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION AMBIGUITY, not resolved this session. tatarica.org's 'Gasification' encyclopedia article states: 'Завершение в 1963 г. строительства газопровода Миннибаево–Казань значительно улучшило обеспечение столицы республики газом. В том же году была начата реконструкция данного газопровода под продуктопровод сжиженных газов, который в 1964 г. был принят к эксплуатации, а в 1965 г. ... впервые в стране был освоен трубопроводный транспорт сжиженных газов на дальние расстояния' -- i.e., the SAME YEAR (1963) the newer gas line was completed, reconstruction of 'this pipeline' (антецедент ambiguous -- could mean the newly-finished 1963 line, or, more logically from an engineering standpoint, the now-redundant original 1954 line freed up once the new line took over gas-supply duty) into a liquefied-gas PRODUCTS pipeline began, completed 1964, pioneering long-distance LPG pipeline transport in the USSR by 1965. Independently, I confirmed (via url_verifier, both OK/200, both name the pipeline) that a real, CURRENTLY OPERATING 'Магистральный этанопровод «Миннибаево-Казань»' (trunk ethane pipeline) exists today: armtorg.ru (2023-04-21, quoting Tatarstan head Rustam Minnikhanov via Interfax) states this ethane pipeline was 'launched 50 years ago' (i.e. ~1973) and describes an ongoing reconstruction replacing its 530mm pipe with 720mm pipe to raise ethane throughput from Minnibaevsky GPZ to Kazanorgsintez; bt-svap.ru (a construction-notices aggregator) separately lists a project explicitly titled with this ethane pipeline's name. The armtorg-stated ~1973 launch year does not cleanly match either P2340's 1954 start or P5744's 1963 start, so this may be a THIRD, separately-built pipe sharing the corridor/operator/name rather than a converted gas line -- but the tatarica.org LPG-conversion narrative (1963-1965) is also real and unexplained if a wholly separate ~1973 ethane line was built later. I could not reach kazan-tr.gazprom.ru (15s timeout, matches this session's measured conditions for *.gazprom.ru) or its Wayback snapshot (Internet Archive returning session-wide HTTP 503 'temporarily offline' on every attempt) to get Gazprom's own account distinguishing the two/three pipes. Given the shared operator (Gazprom Transgaz Kazan for all), shared corridor name, and shared original-diameter figures (both the gas corridor's energybase page and the ethane pipeline give ~530mm as a legacy diameter), there is a real possibility one of GEM's two 'Minnibaevo-Kazan Gas Pipeline' rows (most plausibly the OLDER 1954 line, P2340, given tatarica's 1963-conversion narrative) no longer carries natural gas today -- but I found no direct evidence P2340 has been retired or converted, only evidence that the CURRENT (post-2012) 'existing operating gas pipeline' sources all specifically describe the 1963 line (P5744) instead of the 1954 line. Recording as a flagged concern rather than a reclassification, per standing instruction.
